chunk_text: According to Uttara Kalamrita, if a birth occurs within 48 minutes of Dinardha (mid-day) or Nisardha (mid-night), a king is born who will conquer his enemies, observe religious rules, and be learned.
If an exalted planet is in the 2nd house, in aspect to another exalted planet, a Koteeswara is born.
If an exalted planet is in the 2nd house and is aspected by a planet in its own house, the native will be a Lakshadheri, possessing relatively less riches.

A Raja yoga is formed if the Moon and Venus are mutually in the 3rd and 11th houses from each other. A separate Raja yoga is formed if the Moon and Venus are placed anywhere but mutually aspect each other.
Should the Moon, endowed with strength, be in Vargothamsa and be aspected by four or more planets, the native will become a king.
One will become a king if the ascendant is in Uttamamsa and is aspected by four or more planets, excluding the Moon.
If one, two, or three planets are in their exaltation signs, a person of royal lineage will become a king, while another person will be equal to a king or wealthy.
If four or five planets occupy their exaltation or Moolatrikona signs, even a person of humble origins will become a king.
If six planets are exalted, the native will become an emperor and enjoy various kinds of royal paraphernalia.
If at least one planet among Jupiter, Venus, and Mercury is in exaltation, while a benefic planet is in an angle (Kendra house), the native will become a king or be equal to one.

If all benefic planets are in the angles (Kendra houses 1, 4, 7, 10) while all malefic planets are in the 3rd, 6th, and 11th houses, the native will ascend the throne, even if born into a humble family.

If the 10th lord is conjunct with or aspected by the dispositor of the Amatyakaraka, the native will be a chief in the king's court. The same result occurs if the 10th lord is conjunct with or aspected by the Amatyakaraka planet itself.
